questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I’ve always wanted to live in an English-speaking country outside of Europe for some time. I had been to Canada before and really liked the nature, as well as the friendliness of the people. Further, the University of Toronto has a good reputation and Toronto, being a big and very diverse city, seemed like a cool city to live in for a few months.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really loved the vibe of the city, I found some really nice friends and went on some cool trips; however, I did not like the university system very much, as uni involved a lot of homework, quizzes, and mandatory attendance – which reminded me too much of highschool.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy, I would say. I found everything I needed to know regarding arrival on the university website, and the international office even held 2 online information meetings for exchange students (I think one about housing and one about general information about the exchange) before arrival. There was another information meeting in person after arrival organized by the international student office.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not need any assistance, but you could always email the international office or stop by in person if you have questions or need help.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I did a 2-month internship (in July & August) in Toronto before the start of the exchange semester. For that period of time I found a room via a Facebook housing group. For the period of the exchange semester I rented an Airbnb with another exchange student that I met through a Facebook group.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I’d say it’s pretty hard to find reasonably priced housing. It is a good idea to join Facebook groups and check the UofT housing website (but watch out for scams!)! There is also a pretty popular and relatively cheap private student residence, called Tartu college. If you’re interested, make sure to apply as soon as the application portal opens, since it fills up quickly (I applied about a month later and it was already full). Another option is co-op housing, which exchange students can also apply for and is usually quite cheap.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The price range for housing is very large and it is much easier to find housing for an entire school year (than for 1 semester).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As far as I know, the university doesn’t offer dorms for exchange students staying just 1 semester. Also, on-campus housing is quite expensive, since you usually have to pay for a meal plan as well.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Quite easy. The host university sends emails to all exchange students with Google Docs for course registration, along with instructions on how to fill them out. There are usually 3-4 rounds of registration, so you can still change, add, or drop courses in later rounds. You can find the list of available courses on your host faculty’s website!

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Please check my answer for question 9:)

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can write emails if you have any questions and, as mentioned before, the course registration emails contained detailed instructions on how to fill out the course registration forms.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all 4 courses I wanted!

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would register for all courses you want in the first round since courses may already be full in later registration rounds.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
On the positive side, the teachers were really engaged and enthusiastic about their subjects. You could always approach them with questions, and they always tried to help. They also encouraged students to attend office hours.
On the downside, as I mentioned before, the system felt a bit too much like high school for me - I personally prefer the Danish university system.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: 2 of the courses I took (ECO310 and ECO439) were comparable to the level at UCPH. The other 2 courses were easier, especially since they did not involve many models or (complicated) math and focused more on just learning by heart.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In Toronto I had mandatory attendance, regular quizzes, homework, and assignments. Your final grade didn’t just depend on one exam at the end of the semester (like at UCPH), but also on things like assignments, quizzes, homework, attendance, and a midterm. Because of that, the workload during the semester was higher, but the pressure at the end was lower since the final exam didn’t count for your entire grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: ECO 310 Empirical Industrial Organization / ECO333 Urban Economics / ECO369 Health Economics / ECO439 Empirical Methods in Microeconomics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I really enjoyed ECO310. It is a great course if you are into industrial organization, because you learn the theory and then actually apply it using datasets and STATA. The professor also gives you past exams and assignments (with solutions), which makes studying for the midterm, final, and the 2 assignments much easier.
I would also recommend ECO333 if you are looking for a relatively easy course. The lecturer was really nice and easy to follow.
Even though the professor for ECO369 was very good – she is really good at presenting and the content was interesting – I did not like the course that much. It was mostly about learning by heart, and I personally prefer courses with more models and calculations.
ECO439 had really interesting content and the professor was nice, but the slides were very theoretical and sometimes hard to understand. There were no regular problem sets (just two assignments), and we only got one past exam without solutions to prepare for the final, which made studying quite difficult.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Maybe that I had to buy a book for one of my courses (&textbooks are usually quite expensive!)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Phone plans are quite expensive. Getting a coffee is quite cheap (which is why often went to cafes).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are many varsity games that you can watch for free as a UofT student. There are also numerous sports clubs you can join! I, for example, went to the run club sometimes.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many! As mentioned before, there are many student clubs you can join. Also, the international office organized a few social events for exchange students, such as watching a varsity American football game, a trivia night or pumpkin carving.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would go watch a varsity game (I went to an American football game as well as an ice hockey game) and I liked the run club where you get to go for a run and socialize with other students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit the Niagara falls (it’ll be easy to find other exchange students to go with, as everyone wants to visit the falls). Further, I went on a roadtrip to the Algonquin Provincial park; the nature is absoluteliy worth a visit! You could also do trips to Alberta (visit the Rocky Mountains, Banff etc.) or Montreal and Quebec city. I also went to St. John’s in Newfoundland with a friend for a couple of days (very cute town and pretty nature but very rainy!!). There is so much to see in Canada!! You also get a week off from uni in October (“reading week”) which you can use for traveling; I used it to travel to Cancun in Mexico, which I can recommend as well! In general, there are many cheap flights from Toronto to destinations in the US or Mexico.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy; it’s very similar to European culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Speak to students in your classes and join student clubs. Canadians are generally very open:)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Canada/generally North America is made for cars! Compared to other North American cities, the public transport system (you have TTC in Toronto and GO Transit in the Greater Toronto Area) in Toronto is well developed and relatively reliable, however, if you would like to visit provincial parks or smaller towns outside of Toronto it can get tricky or even impossible to get there without a car.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I felt very welcome! Canadians are very friendly:)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Join the UofT Facebook group for exchange students as well as Whatsapp groups. Exchange students will use these groups to organize events:)
2. Register for the courses you want in the first registration round!
3. Visit some nature!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Like I said before, join Facebook and Whatsapp groups! That helps a lot to meet people!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Finding nice friends and visiting pretty parks near Toronto!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding housing, I would say?

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: noo

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
